messages:
Rae (sales): NovaHealth follow-up: they want SNI exposed to their DMZ TLS inspector AND original client IPs in app logs for compliance. They also want a 1-line monthly cost delta for ~5TB to include in the SOW. Recommend peering or PrivateLink?

Diego (solutions): Short: Peering keeps src IP and lets their inspector see SNI without extra proxies. PrivateLink isolates access (good for teams that forbid peering) but endpoint ENIs become apparent source IPs; client IPs are lost unless they terminate TLS at their proxy and forward X-Forwarded-For.

Samir (netops): Quick topology notes:
- Peering: TGW/spoke -> peering -> redwood-vpc -> app (no NAT; src IP preserved)
- PrivateLink: TGW/spoke -> interface endpoint -> ENI -> redwood (src = endpoint IP)

Samir (netops): Firewall snippets to hand ops:
```
# PrivateLink
Allow TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>
# Peering
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>
# Common
Enforce TLS >= 1.2; deny weak ciphers
Log X-Forwarded-For if proxy terminates TLS
```

Ivy (security): For questionnaire/KMS item: "Redwood Private supports integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM. Customer keys are not stored plaintext; key usage is audited and exportable. Mutual TLS and customer CA support available; rotation policies configurable." Also: "If TLS inspection is required in-customer DMZ, TLS must be terminated on customer proxy and re-established to Redwood."

Rae (sales): One-liner cost delta for SOW please (very rough).

Diego (solutions): Ballpark numbers: PrivateLink infra ~ endpoint ~$0.01/hr + data processing ~$0.01/GB -> ~ $50-70/mo for 5TB (excl cloud egress). Peering: no endpoint/data-processing fee; cross-VPC transfer ~$0.005-$0.02/GB -> ~$25-100/mo. Peering often cheaper at scale but needs peering approvals and route updates.

Samir (netops): Ops effort note: Peering requires cross-account peering + route table updates (estimate 1-2 engineer-hours) and security review. PrivateLink typically faster sign-off (no route exchange) but needs endpoint allowlist and may need proxy logic for client IPs.

Rae (sales): Can we support a hybrid (both SNI inspection and preserved client IP) without big infra changes?

Diego (solutions): Hybrid approach: deploy a small customer-side TLS proxy that terminates for the DMZ inspector, then re-TLS to Redwood over peering, and preserve client IP via X-Forwarded-For header. That keeps SNI visible to DMZ and lets backend correlate client IPs. Document as engineering integration task in SOW.

ticket-bot: Created RW-4411: "NovaHealth POC - network decision, SOW cost delta, and runbook" and attached runbook stub.

Rae (sales): Perfect. Please paste a 2-sentence SOW blurb I can drop into the doc.

Diego (solutions): SOW blurb: "Recommendation: For the NovaHealth POC we recommend VPC peering to Redwood Private when visibility of SNI to an inline TLS inspector and preservation of original client IPs are required, as peering preserves network source IPs and allows DMZ inspection without proxy re-termination. If cross-account peering is not permitted, PrivateLink is an alternative but requires TLS termination at the customer proxy (or X-Forwarded-For insertion) and incurs modest per-GB interface processing fees; engineering onboarding will include an ops checklist and firewall allowlists."

Rae (sales): Thanks all 44d — I'll include that and wait for customer choice.
